niche: an area control centre's summer traffic plan: whether any en-route sector will run over the safety plan's tolerance of ATM-related losses of separation per 100,000 flight hours in summer 2027, when a new low-cost base sends its departures climbing and arrivals descending through a busy east-west trunk airway

driver: Events arise when one moving unit passes through the position of another present at the same time, so the expected count follows the crossings a period's traffic creates rather than the time units spend, their number or its square; a forward change that sends new units across a dense existing flow multiplies the crossings while barely adding time, so scaling last period's events by time spent, by counts, by their square or by the time spent changing position keeps a unit under a rate limit that its crossings carry over it.
driver_concrete: Losses of separation in the Holmvik centre happen where one aircraft climbs or descends through the level of another in the same sector (every one of the 96 ATM-related losses in the record), so each sector's summer 2027 losses follow the pairs whose levels change order in the summer 2027 planning traffic; Brekka's new base sends 26 departures and 26 arrivals a day climbing and descending through Tarvik's trunk-airway cruise levels, adding about 10 per cent to its flight hours and multiplying its pairs five-fold, which takes it to 72.4 against the safety plan's 40.0 losses per 100,000 flight hours while every other sector stays at or under 26.4.
stump: A competent solver keeps each sector's summer 2026 losses of separation per 100,000 flight hours, scales each sector's losses with its 2027 flight hours from the planning traffic and files that no sector reaches the safety plan's 40.0 in summer 2027 (Mosby highest at 32.0, Tarvik 13.4); the step that lands it there is forecasting losses from flight hours when separation is lost where one aircraft climbs or descends through another's level, so the Brekka flights that add about 10 per cent to Tarvik's flight hours multiply its pairs whose levels change order five-fold (9,682 to 48,545) and take it to 72.4, every other sector at or under 26.4.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who keeps the ATM-related losses of separation, attributes each to its elementary sector, reads the season in local time and computes summer flight hours exactly still forecasts summer 2027 by scaling each sector's losses with its flight hours, with the square of its traffic or with its climbing and descending flight hours, and files that no sector exceeds 40.0, because only counting the vertical crossings in each sector shows the new Brekka flights taking Tarvik over the tolerance.
domain_test: What decides the call is air traffic control's human-factors safety analysis of controller workload: a loss of separation is a controller error in a vertical interaction (one aircraft cleared through the level of another), so a sector's expected losses follow the vertical crossings in its traffic, a complexity measure the field uses beside flight hours; with another field's nouns there are no flight levels to cross and no climb through a cruising flow, so the task does not survive the swap.

lineage.driver: When events arrive both from a steady background and in short self-exciting runs, each run a burst of events close in place and time that ends once it has played out, a unit's recent count overstates its coming count exactly where a run has just passed, so the coming count follows the unit's background rate, which only separating the run events (each within a short distance and interval of an earlier one) from the rest recovers; projecting whole counts by any persistence, seasonal or smoothing rule names a unit whose run is over instead of the unit whose background has risen.
